Playing it

ControlWhat it does
6 top buttonschoose channel 1–6 (lit: chosen; glowing: sounding). On a channel's page, another channel shows the same page; the chosen channel again: its main view. From any other page, back to the channel.
SELECT knobthe chosen channel's LEVEL: its fader. In most loops it is what makes them sing. 1 dB a detent up to −5 dB, then 0.1 dB a detent (−4.9, −4.8 …) up to +12 dB, where a loop's edge is. Below −60 dB: off.
ALGORITHM knobits PAN, one step a detent, L 50 … R 50. In a no-input mixer the pan shapes the sound, not only its place: in a loop through the mix bus it is part of the loop.
KNOB 1–4on the main view: GAIN, FREQ (the middle filter's), LIMIT (the loop's pitch), SEND 1; with SHIFT: NOISE, MID (the middle filter's gain or width), PROTECT (the overload protection), SEND 2. A dial covers the screen while you turn. On a page: its four rows.
OCT− / OCT+the channel's pages: MAIN, AMP, NOISE, EQ, SEND, FX (on SEQ's pages: through those). Their lights: a page that way.
SHIFT held on a pageits rows show the page's switches (FX: IN, OUT, LO-FI, BYPASS; EQ: FILTER, MIDDLE; OUT: SPACE): SHIFT + KNOB 1–4 set them.
SEQCOMPRESSOR, OUT, OUT EQ, OUT FX, then the chosen channel's motion: LFO 1, LFO 2, MOD 1 TO 4, MOD 5 TO 8; then back to the channel's page. On LFO and MOD pages a channel's button shows the same page for that channel.
SHIFT + SEQthe chosen channel's modulation thrown anew: both LFOs and two to four slots, at random.
ARPthe OVERVIEW: the six channels, their inputs and levels at once.
HOMEa new patch from any recipe (see New patches).
SHIFT + HOMEa new patch from the recipe named in the main view: the one playing, or the one PRESETS turned to.
HOME held 0.8 sthe patch nudged: every channel's tone moved a little, its connections and levels kept.
PRESETS knobthe recipe, from the one playing: its name in place of the patch's, in the main view; nothing else changes until SHIFT + HOME. On the MOD pages: where the slot comes from; on the RHYTHM's: the styles.
SAVEthe SNAPSHOTS page (again: back): see Snapshots.
SAVE heldsave the session: over the one loaded, at once; otherwise a new one (asked: PRESETS chooses NO or YES, SAVE answers).
SHIFT + SAVEthe SESSIONS page: PRESETS chooses, SAVE loads. Held 0.8 s: GLOBAL SETUP.
RECarm the chosen channel's gesture loop; REC again ends it and it plays. Held 1 s: empty it. See Gestures.
PLAYthe chosen channel's gesture loop played, or stopped (lit while it plays).
SHIFT + PLAYthe output muted, or back (OUT MUTED on the screen). The loops keep going, unheard.
White keys 1–15the chosen channel's INPUT: PRE, POST, MIX L, MIX R, SEND 1, SEND 2, RET 1, RET 2, NONE, CH 1 … CH 6 (lit: the one it has).
White key 16its MAIN MIX on or off.
Black keys 1–6mute channels 1–6 (lit: muted).
SHIFT + black key 1the chosen channel at random: every parameter — its input, voice, filters, sends, slot, LFOs and matrix, fader and pan (set so it sings); its mute kept.
Black key 10 (2nd from the right)the RHYTHM on or off (the first time: one drawn). Its light: on while it plays, dark a moment on each beat.
SHIFT + black key 10a new rhythm, of another style, playing.
Black key 10 held 0.8 sthe TEMPO page (again: back). See Rhythm.
Black key 9 (3rd from the right)the DRUMS pages (again: back). See Drums.
SHIFT + black key 9a new drum rhythm, of another style, playing.
Black key 9 held 0.8 sthe drums on or off. Its light: on while they play.
SHIFT + black key 7, heldthe CPU page.
Black key 11 (last)SHIFT.
MASTER knobthe level after everything.
OCT− and OCT+, held 5 sUBOOT, the chip's own updater.

The main view

The chosen channel's number, very large, in its colour — in grey when the channel is not in the patch (muted, or nothing of it reaches anything: its LEVEL and SENDs off, with no RHYTHM); under it its input; under that the patch's name (or a message, black on white; or MUTED, white on red); its meter, with a white bar where its fader is (red at the left when the fader is down); its pan along the bottom.

A channel

Left to right, as the app's block diagram:

input selector → + noise → GAIN → tube → FOLD → op-amp (and its overload protection) → HIGH, LOW → middle filter → brickwall limiter → mute → SEND 1, SEND 2 → LEVEL → insert effect → PAN → main mix

PageRows (KNOB 1–4)With SHIFT
AMPTUBE, GAIN (0 … +48 dB), FOLD (off, ×1.2 … ×16), OP-AMPKNOB 1: MODE (LINEAR, SATURATED)
NOISENOISE (off, −90 … −18 dB; GEIGER: its clicks' rate), TYPE (WHITE, PINK, RED, CRACKLE, GEIGER, HUM), LIMIT, PROTECT
EQHIGH and LOW (shelves ±15 dB, or cuts), the middle (PEAK ±18 dB, or NOTCH or BAND and their Q), FREQ (30 Hz … 16 kHz)KNOB 1: SHELF or CUT; KNOB 3: PEAK, NOTCH, BAND
SENDINPUT, SEND 1, SEND 2, MAIN MIX
FXthe channel's slot: EFFECT, its two parameters, PRESENCEKNOB 1: IN; KNOB 2: OUT; KNOB 3: LO-FI; KNOB 4: BYPASS
LFO 1, LFO 2SHAPE, RATE (a step a detent), MODE, FADE
MOD 1 TO 4, MOD 5 TO 8the matrix's eight slots, four a page: each row a slot — its number and where it comes FROM, small; where it goes TO and by how much, large; the amount a bar from the middle. KNOB 1–4: the AMOUNT (an amount on an empty slot takes it from LFO 1)KNOB 1–4: TO. PRESETS: FROM, of the slot in hand (the last turned, its row lit)

A page's rows show each parameter's name small, with a bar, and its value large under it. Hold SHIFT to see the page's switches in place of its rows.

The input is what makes the loop:

InputThe loopWhat makes it sing
PREthe channel alone, from after its levelits LEVEL
POSTthe channel and its insert effectits LEVEL; the effect shapes the loop
MIX L / MIX Ra side of the mix bus: every channel feeding it, and the returnsits LEVEL and PAN — and every other channel's
SEND 1 / SEND 2a send bus: every channel feeding itits SEND
RET 1 / RET 2a return bus: through the rack's effects on the sendsits SEND, through the effects
NONEno loop: the noise generator alone, through the channel
CH 1 … CH 6another channel's output (after its insert): channels in a chain or a ringeach channel's LEVEL round the ring

GAIN amplifies the noise and the loop. The tube shapes the sound as it rises (SATURATED drives it harder). The op-amp amplifies it again and adds its own colour: the 741 and OP07 are slow and dark, the 4558 warm, the CA3140 lopsided, the TL072 and NE5532 clean. PROTECT sets the threshold of the overload protection: when the op-amp's signal goes over it, the protection breaks the signal for a few milliseconds and the loop starts again from the noise, with the crackle no-input players know. Higher, it lets more through and the op-amp saturates more.

FOLD drives the signal after the tube into a wavefolder: past full scale it folds back instead of clipping, so the harder it is driven — by FOLD, by GAIN, by a loop growing — the more harmonics, never more level. It changes the timbre only, never the pitch.

LIMIT is the brickwall limiter's speed. Its look-ahead is the delay that sets the base pitch of a loop: fast (a fraction of a millisecond) gives high tones, slow (tens of milliseconds) low ones. The page shows it in milliseconds.

The filters set where a loop rings: a loop sings where its gain is highest, and a peak or a band-pass is where you tune it. A loop can only ring at pitches its delay allows, so a narrow band-pass between them can keep a loop silent.

The rack

Seven slots: slot 1–6 are the channels', slot 7 the output's (OUT FX). A slot's IN is OFF, INSERT (its channel's insert; slot 7: the output's), SEND 1, SEND 2 or PREV (the slot before it); its OUT is NONE, RET 1 or RET 2. An insert's output goes on through its channel, and to a return too if OUT says so.

EffectParameter 1Parameter 2
DELAYTIME (1 ms … 0.37 s; 0.74 s in LO-FI) — turned, it bends the pitch as a tape wouldFEEDBACK
FLANGERDEPTHRATE
CHORUSINTENSITYRATE
TREMOLORATEVIBRATO
FORMANTVOWEL (A E I O U)WIDTH
BITCRUSHALGORITHM (fewer bits; a lower rate; the bits folded on themselves)OFFSET
GLITCHLENGTH of the part that sticksREPEATS
RESONATORROOT, C2 … B5, a semitone a stepCHORD: OCTAVES, FIFTHS, MAJOR, MINOR, SUS, CLUSTER, PELOG, HARMONICS
XMODMODE: RING (a diode ring), XOR (the two signals' bits), FOLD (their sum and product, folded), COMPARE (the louder of the two)WITH: CH 1 … CH 6, MIX L, MIX R, SEND 1, SEND 2
DUCKDEPTHKEY: CH 1 … CH 6, MIX L, MIX R, SEND 1, SEND 2 — the louder it is, the quieter this
GATEDEPTHKEY: as DUCK's — the louder it is, the more this opens
CYCLESMODE: WAVELOSS (the first n of every 8 cycles silent), SPUTTER (a half-cycle now and then turned over or silent), WAVESET (each cycle repeated)AMOUNT
REEDNOTE, C2 … B5, a semitone a stepBREATH
OCTAVERMODE: ONE DOWN, TWO DOWN, BOTHTONE
DIFFUSERSIZE 1 … 8DENSITY
SAGTIME: the window it averages over, 1.5 … 371 msDEPTH
CUTSUNIT, 10 … 46 msDENSITY

RESONATOR is six tuned resonators on the root, in the chord's intervals, ringing about 1.2 s (after 4ms's SMR). In a loop it pulls the feedback onto those notes and holds it there. Its ROOT and CHORD are steps and no LFO can move them: it steadies pitch, never glides it. XMOD (after Mutable Instruments' Warps) and DUCK / GATE (after its Streams) take a second signal, so one loop can shape another: ring-modulate it, mangle its bits, duck it or open it in time with it.

Build 5's six, all steady in pitch: CYCLES works on whole wave cycles between the zero crossings — WAVELOSS drops some in a regular pattern (rhythmic holes a loop rebuilds itself through), SPUTTER turns half-cycles over or silences them at random (crackle), WAVESET repeats each cycle (a time-stretched stutter that sinks into sub-drones). REED is a clarinet's bore and reed (after STK's Clarinet): the signal is its breath, and it blows at its NOTE, which is a step and never moves. OCTAVER adds one or two octaves down, locked to the signal by flip-flops on its zero crossings (after OWL's OctaveDown). DIFFUSER smears transients into a dense, metallic wash (Clouds' diffuser). SAG is a power supply starving (after Airwindows' PowerSag2): loud a while, the gain sinks and comes back, so loops pulse and breathe; TIME is how long it remembers. CUTS cuts the sound into phrases (3 3 2, 2 2 2 2 and the like); a cut plays on, or repeats what came just before it, whole or in halves or quarters — structured stutters after BBCut and Livecut. GLITCH is unchanged.

PRESENCE is how much of the effect is heard; LO-FI halves its rate and its bits.

The output

PageRowsWith SHIFT
COMPRESSOR (SEQ's first)AMOUNT (OFF .. 100 %), THRESH, RELEASE, SIDECHAIN (KICK or OFF)ATTACK, RATIO (2:1 .. 20:1, AMOUNT's share of it)
OUTLEVEL (the main level), RET 1, RET 2, SPACE MIXKNOB 4: the SPACE (ROOM, HALL, PLATE, CAVE, ABYSS, VOID)
OUT EQHIGH, LOW, GAIN, FREQKNOB 1: SHELF or CUT; KNOB 3: WIDE or NARROW
OUT FXslot 7, as a channel's FX pageas there

The COMPRESSOR works on the mixer's sound, before the drums join it, to hold its own against them. AMOUNT does it all at once: it compresses (that share of RATIO) and makes up the gain, so the mix comes forward, and with SIDECHAIN on KICK it ducks the mix under each kick (up to 18 dB) and lets it back over RELEASE: low AMOUNT, a little lift and a gentle pump; high, the mix up front and a deep pump. Measured on the host with a drawn patch: 35 % brings the mix 5.6 dB forward and ducks it 4.7 dB under the kick; 90 %, as far forward (the output's headroom) and 12 dB under the kick. OFF leaves the mix untouched. A session keeps it; HOME does not touch it.

At the top, SPACE MIX leaves the reverb alone.

New patches

As on Tonitor: HOME draws a new patch from any recipe, so each press can be anything; SHIFT + HOME draws one from the recipe named in the main view. That is the playing patch's recipe, or another: PRESETS turns through them from it, the name changing in place. Lilliput starts with a patch drawn from any recipe and a tempo drawn between 91 and 299 BPM, otherwise each time; a session loaded names its patch's recipe. A recipe is an archetype, not a preset: a kind of no-input sound, each with its own way of connecting the channels, its own register, filters, tubes, op-amps, noises, effects and space — and its own motion, LFOs on the parameters that make its character, drawn anew for each channel. Every draw comes out otherwise, in the recipe's direction:

RecipeWhat it isHow it moves

Only what makes it sound is kept: two channels heard at least, the faders past where the loops singeach gesture to a destination drawn for each channel

HOME draws from any recipe; SHIFT + HOME from the one named. The patch's name, on the main view, is its recipe's.

The faders are set a little past where each loop starts to sing, so a patch sounds at once and the faders are where the playing is. Some channels come with their fader down: brought up, they join in. For its first two seconds Lilliput plays into a new patch as a player would: a channel whose fader is up but which stays silent has its GAIN raised until it sings. Then it listens to the output and sets the main LEVEL so that every patch comes out about as loud, its peaks under −4 dB. After that a guard stays on: if the output holds at its ceiling, the main LEVEL comes down a dB at a time. The faders are never touched.

HOME held 0.8 s moves every channel's GAIN, NOISE, filters, LIMIT and PROTECT a little, the connections and levels kept: the same patch, elsewhere.

Modulation

Each channel has two LFOs and eight slots (Tonitor's modulation matrix, twice its slots). An LFO has a SHAPE (SINE, TRI, SAW UP, SAW DN, SQUARE, STEPS — a new random value each cycle —, DRIFT — smooth random), a RATE (0.01 … 20 Hz), a MODE (FREE; ONSET: from the start each time the channel's loop bursts into sound; ONCE: one cycle from each onset) and a FADE (in over up to 10 s from an onset). A slot takes a source — LFO 1, LFO 2, LEVEL (the channel's own loudness: a loop that moves itself as it grows), OUTPUT (the whole mix's), RANDOM (drawn at each onset) — to a destination — GAIN, NOISE, FREQ, MID, HIGH, LOW, LIMIT, PROTECT, LEVEL, PAN, SEND 1, SEND 2, the channel's slot's two parameters and its mix, or either LFO's rate — by an amount, −100 … +100. The panel's values stay where you set them; the sound moves round them. Every new patch comes with its family's motion; SHIFT + SEQ throws the chosen channel's modulation anew.

Rhythm

The RHYTHM turns the mixer into a rhythmic noise machine: it plays the channels in time — gating them, choking them, striking them, pushing them — in structures drawn from a wide palette of styles.

Each channel gets a lane: its steps (up to 32), its step's length (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8 triplets, 1/16, 1/16 quintuplets, 1/16 triplets, 1/32), its hits and accents, how long a hit holds, how far the gate closes, each hit's chance, its chance of a roll (2 to 4 hits in a step) and its mutation (its steps flipping now and then, each round). Lanes of different lengths drift against each other (polymeter); lanes of different step lengths run in different time (polyrhythm). A lane plays its channel one of four ways:

  • CHOP — what you hear is gated: mutes and unmutes in time. The loop rings on behind the gate.
  • CHOKE — the loop itself is gated: it dies between the hits and grows back on each, a swell.
  • KICK — the loop is choked, and struck at each hit by a burst of noise, pushed past its edge (+6 dB) while it is open: the loop's own sound made a drum.

A channel in a ring (it takes another channel, or another takes it) is never choked: CHOKE and KICK gate what is heard instead, so the ring runs on behind the gate (choked, it died and never came back).

  • ACCENT — no gate: each hit pushes GAIN and FOLD up for a moment. A drone pulses in timbre, never in pitch.

SHIFT + the 2nd black key from the right draws a new rhythm for the patch as it is: the darkest loop gets the kick's part, the brightest the hats', those between the snare's and the percussion's; a channel with its fader down is left out, and now and then a drone is left free under it all. A loop slow to grow (a slow limiter, a narrow band-pass, a loop through the sends) is chopped rather than choked. A sparse lane — open a fifth of the time or less — is chopped too, over a bed 14 dB down, so its channel is never all but silent. Every recipe with every style sounds (the host's test plays them all). The styles:

Style
INDUSTRIALfour on the floor, the backbeat, off-beat hats
POWER NOISE4/4 kicks, a drone chopped in sixteenths, accents
BROKENsyncopated Euclidean kicks and snares (Toussaint's evenly spread hits), swung

POLYMETERlanes of 16, 12, 10, 9, 7, 5, 3 steps against each other
POLYRHYTHMquarters against triplets against quintuplets against eighths
MARCHsnare rolls, ratchets, a military kick
HALFTIMEslow and heavy, long gates
GABBERa kick on every beat, noise bursts between

CHOPdrones chopped in sixteenths and thirty-seconds, holes by chance
TRIBALtresillo, cinquillo, clave, the 12/8 bell

The TEMPO page (the key held 0.8 s): its title is the style playing (or RHYTHM OFF).

KNOB
1TEMPO, 10 … 500 BPM: a BPM a detent, five when turned fast
2SWING: the off steps late, up to a third of a step
3CHAOS: hits skipped, ghost hits added
4LENGTH: every gate shorter or longer (100 %: as drawn)

The MIX page (OCT+ from TEMPO, OCT− back): MIX sets how much of the gates is heard, against the loops as they run on: 100 % all gate (as before), 0 % the loops alone, the rhythm unheard. KICK's bursts and ACCENT's pushes follow it too.

A new patch keeps the rhythm playing (its lanes stay with the channels); snapshots and sessions keep their own. The rhythm's changes — on, off, a new one, the tempo — are gestures like any other: the gesture loop records them.

Drums

A drum section beside the mixer, in the spirit of Bram Bos's Ruismaker Noir: synthesized, punchy and dirty, for rhythmic noise. Four voices — KICK, SNARE, HATS, PERC (struck metal) — of one engine, each with its own lane of steps, on the RHYTHM's tempo and beat. Started, or given a new rhythm, they come in on the next beat; the RHYTHM's changes never disturb them, nor theirs the RHYTHM.

Black key 9 (3rd from the right), short, opens their pages (again: back); held 0.8 s, they start or stop; SHIFT + it draws a new drum rhythm and plays it. On their pages:

  • white keys 1–4 choose KICK, SNARE, HATS, PERC (lit: the one chosen); SHIFT + one draws a new sound for it, from its recipes; held 0.7 s, it is muted (its key blinks, dim; its page says MUTED), held again, back;
  • PRESETS goes through the drum rhythms, a new one of each, playing;
  • OCT− / OCT+ through the three pages.
PageRows (KNOB 1–4)With SHIFT
a voice (its name and its sound's)TUNE (Hz), DECAY, DRIVE, LEVELSWEEP (how far above the pitch it starts), ATTACK (HARD: the sharpest transient; up to 100 ms: a soft one), NOISE (tone or noise), REVERB (its send into SPACE)
its second pageBEND (how fast the sweep falls), COLOR (the noise filter), CLICK (a burst on the hit), PANMETAL (the tone made metallic: off or six ratios), FILTER (low-, band- or high-pass)
the drums' (their rhythm's name)SWING

A voice: a tone, swept down in pitch, and noise through a filter, mixed by NOISE; an envelope rising over ATTACK and falling over DECAY; a CLICK on top; then DRIVE, a tanh up to 32 times over: every voice has its own. The dry drums go to the output after the reverb, so SPACE never washes them away; each voice's REVERB sends it into SPACE's reverb, heard even when the mixer's SPACE MIX is down. Their level is their own: the trim that sets the mixer's main level never moves it.

Sounds (SHIFT + a voice's white key draws one, its values anew each time): kicks DEEP, PUNCH, GABBER, SOFT (a slow attack), TOM, SUB, CRUNCH; snares SNAP, NOISE, BODY, METAL, RIM, CRUSH, LONG; hats CLOSED, OPEN, METAL, SHAKER, TICK, CYMBAL, DIRT; percussion ANVIL, PIPE, SHEET, CLANK, CHAIN, SPRING, GRIND.

Rhythms, after the genre — rigid, militaristic 4/4 from a distorted kick, the strangeness in accents, ghosts and metal rather than in denser kicks — every lane in sixteenths, a bar or two, so the pace is always the tempo's: POWER 4/4, PISTON (eighth-note kicks, the beat accented), MARCH, OFFBEAT (the off-beat crushed hat, a low tom), RUMBLE (a clap on two, a stab, a push every other bar), BROKEN (jagged kicks over a backbeat), 3 AGAINST 4, TRIBAL (toms out of the kick, an anvil on the beat), SHUFFLE (the only one that swings much), DIST BREAK (straight), HALF RITUAL (half time: the hats keep the tempo), BURST FILL (two bars, a noise burst ending the second). As in Noir, a step can be more than a hit: accented, with a pitch of its own, or ALT, its decay cut to a fifth (closed hats among open ones, ghost snares).

The drums are not part of a patch: HOME, the snapshots and the gesture loops leave them alone. A session keeps them.

Gestures

Each channel has its own gesture loop. It records what your hands do to that channel — its knobs, its input key, its mute, its effect slot, the channel thrown at random, a MIDI CC to it — and plays it back, round and round, while you go on playing over it. The loops are independent: each its own length, each started and stopped on its own. REC and PLAY act on the chosen channel, and their lights show its loop.

  • REC arms the channel's loop (the screen says ARMED, REC blinks; its loop, if it plays, stops). Nothing is recorded until the channel changes: its first change starts the recording (REC on the screen, white on red, with the seconds; REC lit). A loop it had is replaced: there are no overdubs, one loop a channel.
  • REC again ends it: the loop is as long as from that first change to now, and plays at once (PLAY lit).
  • PLAY stops it, or plays it again from its start. Stopped, the channel stays where the loop left it.
  • REC held 1 s empties it.

One channel records at a time: REC on another channel ends the recording (it plays) and arms that one. Each round begins from the channel as it was when its recording began — only what the loop touches — so it plays the same way every time; what you change that the loop does not touch stays yours. A new patch or a session stops the loops (PLAY plays each again, over the new mixer). Up to 2048 changes among all the loops, ten minutes each. The output's, the output slot's and the RHYTHM's settings belong to no channel and are never recorded. The loops are kept with the session; a session saved before build 12, with one loop for all, loads as a loop for each channel it touched.

Snapshots

Sixteen complete states of the mixer — every channel, every slot, the output, the modulation — kept with the session. SAVE (short) opens the SNAPSHOTS page: the sixteen as the white keys lie, the stored ones filled, the last recalled framed.

  • a white key let go soon: its snapshot recalled;
  • held 0.8 s: the mixer stored in it;
  • SHIFT + it: emptied;
  • KNOB 1: the MORPH time, off … 30 s. A recall then glides every value that can glide — levels, pans, gains, noise, filters, sends, limiters, protection, the effects' parameters, the returns, the main level — from where it is to the snapshot's; the rest (inputs, types, routings, LFOs) changes at once.

SAVE again, or a channel's button, goes back.

Sessions

SAVE held saves the whole mixer as a session (64 of them); SHIFT + SAVE opens the sessions. A session keeps every parameter, the channel chosen, the patch's name and family, its sixteen snapshots and its gesture loop.

Global setup and MIDI

SHIFT + SAVE held 0.8 s opens GLOBAL SETUP: MIDI (each channel's IN and OUT channel, AUTO for the chosen channel, CC in and out on or off, the USB and TRS ports), AUDIO (USB audio: STEREO, the output, or CHANNELS, the six channels each mono). A channel answers to and sends these CCs: 7 LEVEL, 10 PAN, 16 GAIN, 17 FREQ, 18 LIMIT, 19 SEND 1, 74 MID, 91 SEND 2, 92 NOISE.
